name: Amar Singh
role: Jagdishpur rebel commander and successor to Kunwar Singh
contribution: Amar Singh continued the Jagdishpur resistance after the death of his brother Kunwar Singh and remained a rebel commander in Bihar during the 1857 uprising.
context: His leadership belongs to the Bihar theatre of the wider 1857–1859 rebellion, where local landholding power, military alliances, and resistance to East India Company rule shaped the conflict.
impact: Amar Singh's career shows how the rebellion continued through regional commanders after its best-known leaders were lost. He is remembered as part of the Jagdishpur coalition that challenged Company authority.
highlight: Kunwar Singh's successor who continued the Jagdishpur resistance in Bihar.
seoTitle: Amar Singh of Jagdishpur: Rebel Commander of 1857
seoDescription: Learn about Amar Singh, the Jagdishpur commander who continued Kunwar Singh's resistance during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
shortAnswer: Amar Singh was Kunwar Singh's brother and successor who continued rebel resistance from Jagdishpur in Bihar during 1857.

faq.question: Who was Amar Singh of Jagdishpur?
faq.answer: He was Kunwar Singh's brother and successor who continued the rebel resistance in Bihar during the 1857 uprising.
